# SnapHost

> SnapHost is an instant file-sharing web app for images and PDFs. Upload a file, get a public
> link in seconds. Works with no account at all: anonymous links auto-expire after 24 hours.

## What SnapHost does

- Accepts PNG, JPG, WEBP, and PDF uploads up to 10 MB per file (50 MB on Pro).
- Returns a public share link immediately after upload.
- Anonymous uploads need no signup; links expire after 24 hours automatically.
- Signed-in users get a dashboard to rename files, change slugs, set per-file expiry, and delete uploads.
- Signed-in users with a username get readable share URLs of the form `snaphost.dev/<username>/<slug>`.
- Pro tier adds unlimited active links, password-protected links, custom expiry, priority CDN, and 50 MB uploads.

## Plans

| Plan | Active links | Max file size | Custom URL | Expiry control | Dashboard |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Anonymous (free) | 3 | 10 MB | No | 24 hours, automatic | No |
| Starter (free) | 5 | 10 MB | Yes | User-controlled | Yes |
| Pro | Unlimited | 50 MB | Yes | User-controlled | Yes |

Pro is activated manually after a payment is confirmed (Digital Wallet or Bank Transfer), typically within 24 hours.

## Technical notes

- Shared file pages live at `/f/<slug>`, `/anon/<slug>`, and `/<username>/<slug>`. These are user-uploaded
  content pages, not marketing content, and expire with the underlying link.
- Authentication and dashboard pages (`/sign-in`, `/sign-up`, `/profile`, `/anon/links`, `/auth/*`) are
  marked `noindex` and excluded from the sitemap.
- Supported types are validated server-side by magic bytes; the declared browser MIME type is never trusted.
